:::{.def}

For this course, we have already installed the required packages, but this section will be important when you want to install packages on your machine or on the Alliance clusters.

:::

## On your own machine

On your machine (but [not on the Alliance clusters](https://docs.alliancecan.ca/wiki/Uv)), I recommend that you use [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) to create a Python project with your chosen Python version and all the necessary packages. `uv` installs packages much faster than `pip`, handles different Python versions extremely smoothly, and resolves dependencies very well.

:::{.note}

If you want more information on this, I gave [a webinar on `uv`](../../tools/wb_uv.qmd) in May 2025.

:::

Create a Python project (let's call it [pt_project]{.codelike}) and `cd` into it:

```{.bash}
uv init --bare pt_project
cd pt_project
```

:::{.note}

`--bare` creates a `uv` project without the files I am not interested in here, such as a [README]{.codelike} and a [main.py]{.codelike}.

:::

Install the packages:

```{.bash}
uv add torch torchvision timm torchmetrics datasets safetensors matplotlib open-clip-torch
```

You will see that the dependencies have automatically populated a [pyproject.toml]{.codelike} file and that a virtual environment called [.venv]{.codelike} was created.

As long as you are within the project, you don't need to activate that virtual environment: all you need to do is run `python`/`jupyter lab`/`ipython`/`ptpython`/a Python script after `uv run`:

```{.bash}
uv run python
uv run jupyter lab
uv run ptpython
uv run my_script.py
```

You can even launch JupyterLab within a project without installing it in that project by using:

```{.bash}
uv run --with jupyter jupyter lab
```

Alternatively, if you really want a `pip` equivalent (for backward compatibility with old pipelines, for instance), you can activate it as you would any other Python virtual environment:

```{.bash}
source .venv/bin/activate
```

### Sharing uv projects

To share your uv project environment (for instance for collaboration), put the [pyproject.toml]{.codelike} and [uv.lock]{.codelike} files under version control (or distribute them to your collaborators by other means): they pin the Python version and the versions of all the installed packages.

A collaborator can recreate the environment (install the proper Python version if missing and install all packages at the pinned versions) by cd-ing into the project and running:

```{.bash}
uv sync
```

## On the Alliance clusters

### Modules

You can look at the list of loaded modules with:

```{.bash}
module list
```

You will of course need a Python module:

```{.bash}
# Look for available Python modules
module spider python
```

```{.bash}
# Look for needed dependencies to load Python 3.14.7
module spider python/3.14.7
```

No CUDA module is required: PyTorch's wheels ship with their own CUDA libraries.

Some of the packages we are using need the Arrow module (if you try to install without loading it, the error message will hint that you need to load it).

::::{.exo}

:::{.yourturn}

Your turn:

:::

- What is the latest available Arrow module?

- What are its dependencies?

- If you want to use [ipython](https://github.com/ipython/ipython) in the terminal for syntax highlighting while prototyping, what do you need to do?

::::

Now that we know which modules to load, let's load them:

```{.bash}
module load StdEnv/2026 python/3.14.7 arrow/26.0.0 ipykernel/2026b
```

### Virtual environment

:::{.note}

I already installed all the necessary packages in the training cluster to save time and space. The instructions for today thus differ from what you would normally do, and the production cluster instructions in the second tab are for your future reference only.

:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Today

I created a virtual Python environment called `pt_env` with all necessary packages under `/project`. All you have to do today is activate it with:

```{.bash}
source /project/def-sponsor00/pt_env/bin/activate
```

### Production cluster

Create a Python virtual environment:

```{.bash}
python -m venv ~/pt_env  # give it the name you want
```

Activate it:

```{.bash}
source ~/pt_env/bin/activate
```

Update pip from wheel:

```{.bash}
python -m pip install --upgrade --no-index pip
```

:::{.notenoit}

Whenever a [Python wheel](https://pythonwheels.com/) for a package is available on the Alliance clusters, you should use it instead of downloading the package from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/). To do this, simply add the `--no-index` flag to the install command.

You can see whether a wheel is available with `avail_wheels <package>` or look at [the list of available wheels](https://docs.alliancecan.ca/wiki/Available_Python_wheels).

Advantages of wheels:

- compiled for the clusters' hardware,
- ensures no missing or conflicting dependencies,
- much faster installation.

If a wheel does not exist on our clusters, you can install it from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/) by omitting the `--no-index` flag for that package, or you can open a ticket so that the wheel be installed.

:::

All the packages needed for this course are available in our wheelhouse:

```{.bash}
python -m pip install --no-index torch torchvision timm torchmetrics datasets safetensors matplotlib open-clip-torch
```

:::

## Moving to the cluster

If you prototyped your project locally and want to move it to an Alliance cluster to run it at scale, here are some tips.

### Environment

Install the packages in a Python virtual environment with `venv` and `pip` as shown above.

### Code

Clone the project from a Git remote (or [copy it with `scp -r` or `rsync`](../../bash/intro_transfer.qmd)):

```{.bash}
scp -r </path/to/local/project> <user>@<cluster>.alliancecan.ca:~/<path/to/remote/project>
```

### Data

EuroSAT contains 27,000 small JPEG files. This is common in deep learning, but clusters are slowed to a crawl by swarms of small files. To bypass this problem, pack the data directory into an archive on your machine and copy the archive to the cluster:

```{.bash}
tar cf data.tar -C </path/to/local/project/data> .
scp data.tar <user>@<cluster>.alliancecan.ca:~/projects/def-<user>/
```

:::{.note}

If the archive is very large, you can use [Globus](../jxai/jxai_getdata.qmd#globus) for the transfer.

:::

Then keep the archive as is on the cluster and only extract it *inside jobs*.
